newsitem.title: UK: UK OFGAS HEAD SAYS NO NEED FOR REGULATORY BOARDS.
newsitem.headline: UK OFGAS HEAD SAYS NO NEED FOR REGULATORY BOARDS.

text.p: The head of Britain's gas industry regulator, Ofgas, told a conference on Wednesday that the current system of one regulator without an executive board was "a very good system".

Clare Spottiswoode told the Strategic Planning Society's conference on "Where are the Utilities Going?" that "having an individual regulator means that decisions can be taken quite fast...(and) I don't happen to think myself that the quality of decision-making would improve if one had a commission".

The Labour party, currently well ahead of the ruling Conservatives in polls with an election scheduled for May 1, has said it would look at the possibility of setting up boards for the industry regulators.
"We can work quite quickly and adapt quite fast to changes," Spottiswoode said in a session which included speakers from regulators in Ontario, Mexico and California.
Having individual regulators "also means the system is easier to keep apolitical", Spottiswoode added.
She said that was important because the "fiscal independence of the regulator would be compromised" if they became involved politically.
Spottiswoode said she did not feel that any change of government after May 1 would impact on the current framework.
She told Reuters that she did not see the Labour party's proposal for a one-off windfall tax on utilities as a criticism of her regulation.
Labour has said it would levy a one-off tax on utilities aimed at raising some three billion stg which would be used for programmes to cut youth unemployment. -- London Newsroom +44171 542 7717
